query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during high-temperature sliding are governed by the formation of a stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface, which acts as a sacrificial layer to reduce metal-to-metal contact and associated wear.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, with a baseline coating thickness of 10 μm and a surface roughness of 0.1 μm
generation.intervention: In situ high-temperature microscopy or synchrotron X-ray diffraction analysis of the coating surface during sliding, with a controlled change in coating thickness to 15 μm and surface roughness to 0.05 μm
generation.conditions: High-temperature sliding regime, with a temperature range of 500-700°C and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s
generation.structural_mediator: Stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface
generation.mechanism: Formation of a sacrificial oxide layer that reduces metal-to-metal contact and associated wear
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% reduction in wear rate and a 15% reduction in microscopic deformation, relative to the baseline coating condition
generation.baseline: Baseline coating condition with a wear rate of 10^-4 mm^3/Nm and a microscopic deformation of 10^-3 μm
generation.boundary: The predicted outcome should hold within the high-temperature sliding regime, with a temperature range of 500-700°C and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance and microscopic deformation may vary depending on the specific coating composition, substrate material, and sliding conditions

falsification_experiment.design: In situ high-temperature microscopy or synchrotron X-ray diffraction analysis of the coating surface during sliding, with a controlled change in coating thickness and surface roughness
measurements: surface oxide layer thickness and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and microscopic deformation do not decrease by at least 10% relative to the baseline coating condition, or if the surface oxide layer is not stable and coherent, then the hypothesis is falsified
